title: The Bill That United the Senate

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日时事通讯

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《DealBook》的商业与政策报道。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市 DealBook 峰会的现场，采访商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的领袖，其中包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zoran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、佐兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的真实对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在 nytimes.com 上对精选采访进行直播，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻报道的一个月免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 我希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is a daily.
sentences.zh: 这是“每日新闻”。

sentences.en: Mr. Romney, aye.
sentences.zh: 罗姆尼先生，赞成。

sentences.en: Is Klobuchar, aye.
sentences.zh: 克洛布查尔女士，赞成。

sentences.en: Mr. McConnell, aye.
sentences.zh: 麦康奈尔先生，赞成。

sentences.en: On Tuesday night...
sentences.zh: 在周二晚上……

sentences.en: The yays are 68.
sentences.zh: 赞成票为68票。

sentences.en: The nays are 32.
sentences.zh: 反对票为32票。

sentences.en: The 60-vote threshold having been achieved, the bill is passed.
sentences.zh: 由于已达到60票的门槛，该法案获得通过。

sentences.en: The United States Senate overwhelmingly passed the kind of historic and sweeping spending bill that typically triggers bitter partisan warfare.
sentences.zh: 美国参议院以压倒性多数通过了一项历史性、全面性的支出法案，这类法案通常会引发激烈的党派争斗。

sentences.en: Today, David Sanger on why this bill did not.
sentences.zh: 今天，大卫·桑格将为我们解析为什么这项法案没有引发争斗。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, June 9th.
sentences.zh: 今天是6月9日，星期三。

sentences.en: David, describe this legislation that was just adopted by the U.S.
sentences.zh: 大卫，请介绍一下美国参议院刚刚通过的这项立法。

sentences.en: Senate.
sentences.zh: 参议院。

sentences.en: Well, Michael, this is, quite simply put, the biggest example of industrial policy that the United States has put together, perhaps in its history, but certainly in many decades.
sentences.zh: 好的，迈克尔，简单来说，这是美国历史上，或者至少是几十年来最大规模的产业政策实例。

sentences.en: And what is industrial policy?
sentences.zh: 什么是产业政策？

sentences.en: Industrial policy, Michael, means using taxpayer dollars to go direct funds to specific industries, research initiatives, or actual manufacturing plants to involve the U.S.
sentences.zh: 产业政策，迈克尔，意味着使用纳税人的钱，将资金直接投向特定行业、研究项目或实际制造工厂，从而让美国

sentences.en: government directly in the private sector economy by injecting massive amounts of capital that, in the normal American way, would be raised first by venture capitalists and then on
sentences.zh: 政府通过注入巨额资本直接参与私营部门经济。而在美国常态下，这些资金通常首先由风险投资家筹集，然后

sentences.en: the stock market.
sentences.zh: 在股票市场上筹集。

sentences.en: And just how much capital are we talking about?
sentences.zh: 我们到底在谈论多少资本？

sentences.en: We're talking about a quarter of a trillion dollars over five years.
sentences.zh: 我们在谈论五年内高达四分之一万亿美元的资金。

sentences.en: So even by Washington standards, that's a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 所以，即使按华盛顿的标准来看，这也是一大笔钱。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's not the first time that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这并不是美国

sentences.en: government has invested in these things.
sentences.zh: 政府第一次投资这些领域。

sentences.en: We do other investments, right?
sentences.zh: 我们也有过其他的投资，对吧？

sentences.en: Like the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency, part of the Pentagon, has been doing this for years.
sentences.zh: 比如五角大楼旗下的国防高级研究计划局，多年来一直在这样做。

sentences.en: But their budget is $3 billion a year.
sentences.zh: 但他们的预算是每年30亿美元。

sentences.en: That's what President Biden asked for for this year.
sentences.zh: 这就是拜登总统今年所要求的预算额。

sentences.en: So it gives you a sense of just how huge an injection of capital in the high tech part of the economy that the Senate bill would require.
sentences.zh: 所以这让你感受到，参议院法案对经济高科技领域的资金注入规模是何等巨大。

sentences.en: And which industries exactly
sentences.zh: 具体是哪些行业

sentences.en: will be invested in under this program?
sentences.zh: 将在该计划下获得投资？

sentences.en: Well, it's everything on the list that you would think of if you picked up the paper and you saw what are the cutting edge industries that the United States worries about.
sentences.zh: 嗯，只要你翻开报纸，看看美国所关心的那些尖端行业，清单上能想到的都在其中。

sentences.en: Semiconductors gets the biggest part of it because the chips that power our computers, our Zoom calls, our automobiles, our refrigerators, and our automated houses.
sentences.zh: 半导体占了最大份额，因为芯片驱动着我们的计算机、Zoom 通话、汽车、冰箱以及智能住宅。

sentences.en: Those are the steel industry of the modern age.
sentences.zh: 它们就是现代社会的钢铁工业。

sentences.en: Autonomous vehicles are a big part of this.
sentences.zh: 自动驾驶汽车是其中的重要部分。

sentences.en: Robotics, artificial intelligence, intelligence.
sentences.zh: 机器人技术、人工智能。

sentences.en: And then, of course, also synthetic biology, basically the creation and manipulation of new organisms and understanding how that process works.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有合成生物学，基本上就是创造和改造新生物，并理解这一过程的运作方式。

sentences.en: There are other areas here.
sentences.zh: 这里还有其他领域。

sentences.en: Quantum computing, which was an entirely different way of going about designing computers at very high speed, critical for
sentences.zh: 量子计算，这是一种以极高速度设计计算机的全新方法，对

sentences.en: defense purposes, for encryption, and perhaps over time for manufacturing.
sentences.zh: 国防目的、加密，以及随着时间的推移可能对制造业都至关重要。

sentences.en: In most of these areas, the bill is pretty vaguely worded about how exactly the money is going to be spent.
sentences.zh: 在大多数这些领域中，法案对资金具体将如何使用措辞相当模糊。

sentences.en: So you know there's going to be a huge scramble now to get a part of this pie by redefining
sentences.zh: 所以你可以预见，现在将会有一场巨大的争夺战，大家要把

sentences.en: projects that are already underway to fit within the categories that Congress has allocated these billions for.
sentences.zh: 已经在进行中的项目重新包装，以符合国会为此拨出巨资的各项类别。

sentences.en: And so, Michael, the big question is, how is it that a U.S.
sentences.zh: 因此，迈克尔，最大的问题是，一个在任何事情上都无法达成一致的美国

sentences.en: Senate that can't agree on anything, that's arguing with President Biden over infrastructure projects and the usual easy stuff
sentences.zh: 参议院，一个正与拜登总统就基础设施项目以及诸如修建公路和大坝之类

sentences.en: like building highways and dams, how is it that they've agreed to spend a quarter trillion dollars on this remarkable array of high-tech industry?
sentences.zh: 寻常简单事情争论不休的参议院，怎么会同意在这组令人瞩目的高科技产业上花费四分之一万亿美元呢？

sentences.en: That's really the great mystery that's been surrounding Washington these past couple of days.
sentences.zh: 这确实是过去几天环绕在华盛顿上空的巨大谜团。

sentences.en: And what is the answer?
sentences.zh: 答案是什么？

sentences.en: Because that very much is the question I have.
sentences.zh: 因为这也是我最大的疑问。

sentences.en: How is it possible that Washington came together for a spending bill this vast?
sentences.zh: 华盛顿怎么可能为如此巨额的支出法案团结起来？

sentences.en: There is one reason and one reason only.
sentences.zh: 原因只有一个，也只有这一个。

sentences.en: It's China.
sentences.zh: 那就是中国。

sentences.en: And what do you mean by that?
sentences.zh: 你这话是什么意思？

sentences.en: Well, China has been spending heavily in this arena, almost this exact same list of research projects and industries since 2015.
sentences.zh: 嗯，自2015年以来，中国一直在这一领域投入巨资，几乎涵盖了与此完全相同的研究项目和产业清单。

sentences.en: They've got a project underway called Made in China 2025.
sentences.zh: 他们正在推进一个名为“中国制造2025”的项目。

sentences.en: And by that deadline, they want to be self-sufficient in all of these territories, from semiconductors to autonomous vehicles to everything else that was on our liSt.
sentences.zh: 根据这一最后期限，他们希望在所有这些领域实现自给自足，从半导体到自动驾驶汽车，再到我们清单上的所有其他内容。

sentences.en: They don't want to have to rely on the United States or the West for any of those technologies.
sentences.zh: 他们不希望在任何这些技术上依赖美国或西方。

sentences.en: And so what's happened here in Washington, Michael, is that the mirror image of the Chinese fear
sentences.zh: 所以，迈克尔，华盛顿这里发生的情况是，

sentences.en: has been playing out on Capitol Hill gradually, where senators are waking up to the thought that the United States is incredibly dependent on China.
sentences.zh: 对中国恐惧的镜像正在国会山逐渐上演，参议员们逐渐意识到美国对中国的依赖程度高得惊人。

sentences.en: We saw it in the argument over 5G networks, where the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我们在关于5G网络的争论中看到了这一点，当时美国

sentences.en: had gotten out of the business.
sentences.zh: 已经退出了该行业的竞争。

sentences.en: We've seen it in semiconductors, where the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我们在半导体领域也看到了这一点，美国在市场中所占的份额比过去小得多。

sentences.en: is a much smaller part of the market than it was.
sentences.zh: 市场份额比过去小得多。

sentences.en: And over time, what this has done is created a bipartisan consensus that no matter what else we agree or disagree on,
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，这形成了一种两党共识：无论我们在其他什么事情上有分歧或达成一致，

sentences.en: we can't be in a position in 2025 where we are dependent on China for the key technologies that keep our industry going and that keep our defense sector going.
sentences.zh: 我们绝不能在2025年陷入这样一种境地：在维系我们工业和国防部门的关键技术上依赖中国。

sentences.en: And somehow that has managed to so seep into the body politic that there was no real debate, especially when people looked at
sentences.zh: 不知何故，这种观念已经深深渗透到政治体制中，以至于没有产生真正的辩论，特别是当人们看到

sentences.en: the sheer numbers and saw that the Chinese government spending on research and development is now twice what the U.S.
sentences.zh: 惊人的数字，发现中国政府在研发上的支出现在已经是美国

sentences.en: spending is as a percentage of GDP.
sentences.zh: 占GDP比例的两倍时。

sentences.en: And that's a big change.
sentences.zh: 这是一个巨大的转变。

sentences.en: David, this bill seems to assume that China's dominance in these industries is a pretty urgent threat.
sentences.zh: 大卫，这项法案似乎认为中国在这些产业中的主导地位是一个相当紧迫的威胁。

sentences.en: And is that true?
sentences.zh: 事实果真如此吗？

sentences.en: Because my sense is that we have relied on China to manufacture all kinds of goods that get exported back to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 因为我的感觉是，很长一段时间以来，我们一直依赖中国来制造各种运回美国出口的商品。

sentences.en: for a really long time.
sentences.zh: 长期以来一直如此。

sentences.en: We have relied on them.
sentences.zh: 我们确实依赖过他们。

sentences.en: But I think what's changed in recent times is the recognition that China is not just an economic competitor and not just that it's a potential military adversary.
sentences.zh: 但我认为近年来的变化是人们认识到，中国不仅仅是一个经济竞争对手，也不仅仅是一个潜在的军事对手。

sentences.en: It's that China has brought about a combination of its military prowess and its economic prowess and made us over time
sentences.zh: 而是中国将其军事实力与经济实力结合起来，随着时间的推移，使我们

sentences.en: increasingly dependent on Beijing for the core technologies that run our economy.
sentences.zh: 越来越依赖北京来获取运营我们经济的核心技术。

sentences.en: And people started asking the question, first, can we really rely on China to provide us with 5G advanced cellular networks?
sentences.zh: 人们开始提出疑问：首先，我们真的能依赖中国为我们提供5G先进蜂窝网络吗？

sentences.en: These are the networks that will be powering not only our cell phones, but our factories.
sentences.zh: 这些网络不仅将为我们的手机提供动力，还将为我们的工厂提供动力。

sentences.en: And across the Obama administration, the Trump administration, and now the Biden administration,
sentences.zh: 在奥巴马政府、特朗普政府以及现在的拜登政府期间，

sentences.en: people came to the same answer, which is, no, we really can't rely on China for 5G because they could turn it off in times of tension.
sentences.zh: 人们得出了相同的答案，那就是：不，我们确实不能在5G问题上依赖中国，因为他们在紧张时期可能会将其关闭。

sentences.en: And then we began to look at semiconductors and ask the question, how reliant do we want to be for the foundational technology of everything we build?
sentences.zh: 然后我们开始审视半导体，并提出疑问：对于我们建造的一切事物的基础技术，我们究竟想要达到多大程度的依赖？

sentences.en: And then we began to look at synthetic biology, an area that the United States pioneered and said, how much do we want to be dependent there?
sentences.zh: 接着我们开始关注合成生物学——这是美国率先开创的领域——并思考我们在该领域要依赖到什么程度？

sentences.en: And what's happened over time is that this concept that the two largest economies in the world were inextricably intertwined is now changing to a
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，原本“世界两大经济体密不可分”这一概念，现在正在转变为

sentences.en: concept that the two largest economies in the world have to be self-sufficient.
sentences.zh: “世界两大经济体必须实现自给自足”的概念。

sentences.en: So the fear is quite simply that one day, if the United States does not invest properly in these
sentences.zh: 因此，人们的恐惧非常简单：如果有一天，美国没有在这些

sentences.en: industries and become self-sufficient in these areas, that we might wake up and find that China has
sentences.zh: 产业中进行适当投资并在这些领域实现自给自足，我们可能会一觉醒来，发现中国

sentences.en: basically turned off our economy through goods we've purchased from them or turned all those technologies against us.
sentences.zh: 通过我们向他们购买的商品基本上关闭了我们的经济，或者将所有这些技术转而用来对付我们。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And they wouldn't even need to turn them off.
sentences.zh: 而且他们甚至不需要真的将其关闭。

sentences.en: All we would need to do is live in the fear that they could turn them off.
sentences.zh: 我们只需要生活在“他们随时可能将其关闭”的恐惧中就够了。

sentences.en: And, you know, members of Congress saw in both classified and unclassified session, some pretty remarkable examples.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，国会议员在保密和非保密会议上都看到了非常惊人的实例。

sentences.en: One is that a few years ago, the United States was bringing in some very large electric transformers, the kind you use to power the electric grid.
sentences.zh: 其中之一是，几年前美国引入了一些非常大型的电力变压器，也就是用于电网供电的那种。

sentences.en: And when they sent them off to one of the national labs for examination, they discovered some hardware inserted in the transformers that was not part of the design
sentences.zh: 当把它们送到某个国家实验室进行检测时，人们发现变压器中插入了一些硬件，这些硬件并不在设计

sentences.en: spec that would have essentially enabled somebody in China to flip these on and off.
sentences.zh: 规格之内，它们基本上可以使中国的人员随时远程开关这些设备。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: That's literally the American nightmare.
sentences.zh: 这简直就是美国的噩梦。

sentences.en: It is indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And then in the telecommunications area, we saw something similar.
sentences.zh: 然后在电信领域，我们也看到了类似的情况。

sentences.en: We saw internet traffic that was running through Chinese controlled elements of the network inside
sentences.zh: 我们发现，流经美国境内受中国控制的

sentences.en: the United States that was mysteriously being routed to Beijing before it came back to the United States and elsewhere in the world.
sentences.zh: 网络节点的互联网流量，在返回美国及世界其他地方之前，被神秘地路由到了北京。

sentences.en: And people started asking the question, why is it that China could, from a base in the United States, route traffic at will back to Beijing?
sentences.zh: 人们开始提出疑问：为什么中国能够从美国的基地出发，随心所欲地将流量路由回北京？

sentences.en: And then as the 5G argument revved up and we were urging allies not to buy the Chinese networks,
sentences.zh: 随后，随着5G争论的升温，我们敦促盟友不要购买中国的网络设备，

sentences.en: we had nothing to offer them because American companies had gone out of the business.
sentences.zh: 但我们却无计可施，因为美国企业已经退出了该行业。

sentences.en: And the accumulation of these examples managed to wipe out 30 years of ideological division
sentences.zh: 这些实例的累积最终消除了参议院内部

sentences.en: inside the Senate over whether the United States should be spending taxpayer money on specific industries in order to stay competitive.
sentences.zh: 长达30年的意识形态分歧——即美国是否应该把纳税人的钱花在特定产业上以保持竞争力。

sentences.en: It was a really remarkable thing because this debate that has gone on for decades just fell silent in the face of Chinese competition.
sentences.zh: 这真的是一件非同寻常的事，因为面对中国的竞争，这场持续了几十年的辩论就这样归于沉寂。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了吗？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你能免费探索《时报》一个月，甚至无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是《纽约时报》的订阅者，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: David, describe this 30-year partisan divide that you just referred to over U.S.
sentences.zh: 大卫，请谈谈你刚才提到的关于美国

sentences.en: government investment in American industry.
sentences.zh: 政府投资美国产业的30年党派分歧。

sentences.en: Where does that come from?
sentences.zh: 这种分歧从何而来？

sentences.en: Well, Michael, it dates back to the 1980s when Japan was the great ascendant economic power.
sentences.zh: 嗯，迈克尔，这可以追溯到20世纪80年代，当时日本是崛起中的经济大国。

sentences.en: And the fear in Washington was that we would become what Andy Grove, the founder of Intel, referred to as a techno colony of Japan.
sentences.zh: 当时华盛顿的恐惧是，我们将变成英特尔创始人安迪·格鲁夫所说的日本“技术殖民地”。

sentences.en: Now, it seems hard to imagine today, but back then, Japanese cars were not only flooding the U.S.
sentences.zh: 现在看来这似乎难以想象，但在当时，日本汽车不仅充斥着美国

sentences.en: market, but consumers were grabbing them up.
sentences.zh: 市场，而且消费者们争相抢购。

sentences.en: You've got Tim Donovan here taking his frustrations out on this 78 Toyota.
sentences.zh: 你看到蒂姆·多纳文在这里把满腔怒火发泄在这辆78年的丰田车上。

sentences.en: And the layoffs in Detroit were huge.
sentences.zh: 底特律的裁员规模极其巨大。

sentences.en: When I was raised in Allen Park, they used to have carnivals, and you'd take a whack at a car, and it was always the biggest sensation.
sentences.zh: 我在艾伦帕克长大时，那里经常有嘉年华，你可以去砸一辆汽车出气，这总是最轰动的节目。

sentences.en: We thought, well, why not a Japanese car?
sentences.zh: 我们当时想，嗯，为什么不买一辆日本车呢？

sentences.en: Meanwhile, of course, the Japanese market.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，当然，日本市场……

sentences.en: They come over here, they sell their cars, their VCRs, they knock the hell out of our companies.
sentences.zh: 他们来到这里，销售汽车、录像机，把我们的公司打得落花流水。

sentences.en: It was quite closed to American goods.
sentences.zh: 而他们的市场对美国商品却相当封闭。

sentences.en: But more importantly, you began to see Japan dominate some of the same industries that we're worried about today, starting with semiconductors.
sentences.zh: 但更重要的是，你开始看到日本主导了我们今天所担心的那些产业，首先就是半导体。

sentences.en: And they were producing memory chips, not the microprocessors that do the thinking, but just what holds memory inside computers, right?
sentences.zh: 他们生产的是内存芯片，而不是进行思考微处理器，仅仅是保存计算机内部记忆的部件，对吧？

sentences.en: And this was long before chips were going into every bit of consumer goods.
sentences.zh: 而这远在芯片被广泛应用于各种消费品之前。

sentences.en: And so what was beginning to happen in Congress was a huge backlash against Japan.
sentences.zh: 因此，国会开始对日本产生巨大的强烈反弹。

sentences.en: And I remember it pretty vividly because I was sent by the New York Times for a wonderful six-year assignment in Japan, starting in 1988, in the midst of this dispute.
sentences.zh: 我对此记忆犹新，因为1988年正值这场争端激化之际，我被《纽约时报》派往日本执行一段为期六年的精彩任务。

sentences.en: And I spent most of my time documenting whether or not the Japanese were, in fact, eating our lunch.
sentences.zh: 我大部分时间都在记录日本人是否真的在抢我们的饭碗。

sentences.en: And what was happening as the Japanese government and the Ministry of Industry and Trade began funding big R&D programs in Japan for many of these same industries.
sentences.zh: 当时发生的情况是，日本政府和通产省开始在日本的大型研发项目中为许多这些相同的产业提供资金。

sentences.en: So, David, what does Congress do in response to this perceived threat from Japan?
sentences.zh: 那么，大卫，国会采取了什么行动来回应这种来自日本的感知威胁？

sentences.en: Well, it did a few things, Michael.
sentences.zh: 嗯，迈克尔，它采取了几项措施。

sentences.en: First, it bailed out automakers like Chrysler that were on the edge of bankruptcy.
sentences.zh: 首先，它救助了像克莱斯勒这样濒临破产的汽车制造商。

sentences.en: That was very controversial, but they went ahead.
sentences.zh: 这非常有争议，但他们还是推进了。

sentences.en: And then it put together a consortium of American semiconductor makers and invested $100 million in government funds in the efforts to revive the entire semiconductor industry.
sentences.zh: 随后，它联合了美国半导体制造商组成的财团，并投入了1亿美元的政府资金，用于复苏整个半导体产业。

sentences.en: That consortium was called Semitech.
sentences.zh: 这个财团被称为 Semitech。

sentences.en: And this was at the end of the Reagan administration.
sentences.zh: 而这发生在里根政府的末期。

sentences.en: It was 1987.
But by the time Reagan was leaving office, this effort to boost government spending in these industries began to create a backlash.
sentences.zh: 但就在里根即将卸任之际，这种加大政府对这些行业支出力度的做法开始引发强烈反弹。

sentences.en: And it opened up a really deep ideological divide about what the role of the American government should be in boosting industries and particularly new high-tech ventures.
sentences.zh: 它引发了关于美国政府在推动产业特别是新兴高科技风险企业中应扮演什么角色的一场深刻的意识形态分歧。

sentences.en: And what is the nature of that political divide?
sentences.zh: 这种政治分歧的本质是什么？

sentences.en: Well, on the one side of the Republicans who said, by and large, this is madness.
sentences.zh: 嗯，一方面是共和党人，他们大体上认为，这简直是疯了。

sentences.en: Government is terrible at picking new technologies.
sentences.zh: 政府在挑选新技术方面糟糕透顶。

sentences.en: This is where the market works beSt.
sentences.zh: 这就是市场发挥作用最好的地方。

sentences.en: The creative destruction of inventing something, finding funding for it, seeing if it takes off.
sentences.zh: 创造性地发明某样东西，为之寻找资金，看它是否能腾飞。

sentences.en: That's what makes American industry the shining example for the rest of the world.
sentences.zh: 正是这一点让美国工业成为世界其他地方的光辉榜样。

sentences.en: And the only thing we will do in interfering in this is waste a lot of taxpayer money and get in the way of that process.
sentences.zh: 而我们在这件事上进行干预的唯一结果，就是浪费大量纳税人的钱，并阻碍这一进程。

sentences.en: And then on the other side with the Democrats who are saying, are you crazy?
sentences.zh: 而另一方面则是民主党人，他们说，你们疯了吗？

sentences.en: We've been doing this for years in the territory of basic research.
sentences.zh: 我们在基础研究领域已经这样做多年了。

sentences.en: The work that created the space program not only landed men on the moon, it created first a military and then a commercial satellite business.
sentences.zh: 创造太空计划的工作不仅把人类送上了月球，它还催生了军用卫星业务，随后又催生了商用卫星业务。

sentences.en: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency gave the seed money for the experiments that started the Internet.
sentences.zh: 国防部高级研究计划局为开启互联网的实验提供了种子资金。

sentences.en: And that if you are going to get people to jumpstart key technologies, the best way to do it is pour some government money into it,
sentences.zh: 如果你想让人们重启关键技术，最好的办法就是向其中注入一些政府资金，

sentences.en: even if you know that some of it's going to be wasted.
sentences.zh: 哪怕你明知其中一部分会被浪费。

sentences.en: That you're going to lose some of it because the overall benefit to American job creation is well worth whatever you might lose over the short term.
sentences.zh: 你确实会损失一部分，因为从长远来看，它对美国创造就业机会的整体效益，远超你在短期内可能损失的任何代价。

sentences.en: And so what does this battle look like throughout the next few decades?
sentences.zh: 那么，在接下来的几十年里，这场博弈是什么样的呢？

sentences.en: Well, it got pretty intense during the Clinton administration when President Clinton wanted to go make some major investments and many Republicans called this socialism.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在克林顿政府时期，这种博弈变得相当激烈，当时克林顿总统想要进行一些重大投资，许多共和党人称这是社会主义。

sentences.en: When President Obama was in office, you may remember that the administration provided some loan guarantees,
sentences.zh: 当奥巴马总统在任时，你可能还记得政府提供了一些贷款担保，

sentences.en: just about $500 million to a company called Solyndra that was working on it.
sentences.zh: 大约5億美元给了一家名为Solyndra的公司，该公司一直在从事相关研究。

sentences.en: I do remember.
sentences.zh: 我确实记得。

sentences.en: Yeah, an interesting technology for solar power and solar panels.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一项用于太阳能和太阳能电池板的有趣技术。

sentences.en: And the thing went bad and went bankrupt, as projects like this sometimes do.
sentences.zh: 结果事情搞砸了，公司破产了，就像这类项目有时会做的那样。

sentences.en: It's a symbol not of success, but of failure.
sentences.zh: 它不是成功的象征，而是失败的象征。

sentences.en: And Mitt Romney, it's also a symbol of how the president thinks about free enterprise.
sentences.zh: 在米特·罗姆尼看来，这也是总统对自由企业看法的象征。

sentences.en: Among others, who's of course running against President Obama during the re-election campaign in 2012, argued that this was a prime example of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 在2012年竞选连任期间与奥巴马总统对决的罗姆尼等人认为，这简直是美国政府试图干预资本主义进程的典型例子，

sentences.en: government trying to interfere in the capitalistic process that made the United States such a powerhouse.
sentences.zh: 正是这种资本主义进程让美国成为了如此强大的经济巨头。

sentences.en: He thinks that government-dominated decisions like this make America stronger.
sentences.zh: 他认为这种由政府主导的决策会让美国变得更强大。

sentences.en: And that Obama had wasted taxpayer money.
sentences.zh: 而奥巴马浪费了纳税人的钱。

sentences.en: They make us weaker.
sentences.zh: 这让我们变得更弱了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Romney's argument was this is classic, wasteful, big government spending, and this is exactly what the private sector was designed to do.
sentences.zh: 罗姆尼的论点是，这是典型的、浪费的、大政府开支，而这正是私营部门原本应该做的事。

sentences.en: And even though Romney lost that election,
sentences.zh: 尽管罗姆尼输掉了那场选举，

sentences.en: it felt like he had landed a pretty significant punch with the example of Solyndra that no doubt Democrats would have understood as something politically risky.
sentences.zh: 但人们感觉他凭借 Solyndra 这个例子打出了相当有力的一拳，毫无疑问，民主党人也明白这在政治上是具有风险的。

sentences.en: That's right, especially because the most effective part of the Republican argument was that oftentimes when the United States spends money on research and development,
sentences.zh: 没错，特别是由于共和党人论点中最有效的部分是，通常情况下，当美国将资金花在研发上时，

sentences.en: what happens is the private sector pulls back saying, why should we spend our shareholder money on this when the taxpayers are going to go fund this research for us for free?
sentences.zh: 发生的情况是私营部门会退缩，他们会说，既然纳税人要免费为我们资助这项研究，我们凭什么要把股东的钱花在这上面？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: The Republican argument is that this becomes a perverse set of incentives in which the government displaces the motivations and the instincts of the private sector.
sentences.zh: 共和党人的论点是，这变成了一种反常的激励机制，政府取代了私营部门的动机和直觉。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that's exactly what some of the critics of Semitech, that semiconductor effort that President Reagan began in 1987.
sentences.zh: 这正是里根总统在1987年启动的那项半导体计划（即 Semitech）的一些批评者所说的。

sentences.en: And by the 1990s, it hadn't accomplished many of its goals and it sort of withered.
sentences.zh: 到了20世纪90年代，它并没有实现其许多目标，并且有点名存实亡了。

sentences.en: And when people look back at it, they discovered that semiconductor companies had, in many cases,
sentences.zh: 当人们回首往事时，他们发现在许多情况下，半导体公司

sentences.en: pulled back on private investment because they thought the government would pay for it.
sentences.zh: 由于认为政府会买单，因而削减了私人投资。

sentences.en: So, David, I guess I'm still a bit confused about why we are not seeing this same partisan fight play out with this Senate plan to spend so much U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以，大卫，我想我还是有点困惑，为什么我们没有看到同样的党派之争在这项旨在花费巨额美国政府资金来对抗中国的参议院计划中上演，

sentences.en: government money to counter China, given that you just explained how almost permanent this battle is in the United States Congress.
sentences.zh: 考虑到你刚才解释了这场斗争在美国国会是多么持久。

sentences.en: Congress, why aren't we seeing much of this accompany this Senate proposal?
sentences.zh: 国会，为什么我们没有看到很多这样的声音伴随这项参议院提案出现？

sentences.en: You know, it's a pretty remarkable change.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是一个相当显著的变化。

sentences.en: And I think the reason really comes down to the difference between Japan as a competitor and China as a competitor.
sentences.zh: 我想原因实际上归结为将日本作为竞争对手与将中国作为竞争对手之间的区别。

sentences.en: Yes, Japan was and remains a major economic competitor to the United States, but it's also our closest ally in the Pacific, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，日本过去是、现在仍然是美国主要的经济竞争对手，但它也是我们在太平洋地区最亲密的盟友，对吧？

sentences.en: It's the centerpiece of the American strategy to contain China's expansion in South Korea and Australia.
sentences.zh: 它是美国在韩国和澳大利亚遏制中国扩张战略的核心。

sentences.en: So Japan never posed the existential threat to the United States that China now does.
sentences.zh: 因此，日本从未对美国构成中国现在所构成的生存威胁。

sentences.en: That's what's happening.
sentences.zh: 这就是正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Japan was a commercial adversary, but not a military adversary, and China's the opposite.
sentences.zh: 日本是商业对手，但不是军事对手，而中国则恰恰相反。

sentences.en: But, you know, Michael, something else happened in the course of this that changed the debate, and that was Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 但是，迈克尔，在此期间还发生了一件改变辩论的事情，那就是唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 你是什么意思？

sentences.en: He walked away from all of the usual Republican ideology on this issue and many others when he made that turn about a year and a half ago at the beginning of the pandemic
sentences.zh: 大约一年半前，在大流行刚开始的时候，他在那个转折点上抛弃了关于这个以及许多其他问题的所有寻常共和党意识形态，

sentences.en: and began describing China not as a potential dealmaker with the United States,
sentences.zh: 并开始将中国描述为不是一个可以与美国做交易的潜在伙伴，

sentences.en: but as its mortal enemy that was hiding the cause of coronavirus and maybe had deliberately launched it in his, you know, imaginings.
sentences.zh: 而是将其视为隐瞒新冠病毒起因、甚至可能在他的想象中故意释放病毒的死敌。

sentences.en: And that cemented the view in his own party that any bill that was described as a counter-China bill was worth passing.
sentences.zh: 这巩固了他自己党内的观点，即任何被描述为反华法案的法案都值得通过。

sentences.en: And when President Biden came in, he actually extended this debate by casting it as the battle between democratic forces and autocracy.
sentences.zh: 而当拜登总统上台后，他实际上通过将这场辩论定性为民主力量与独裁统治之间的斗争，延续了这一辩论。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: There was a line in President Biden's speech to both houses of Congress that spoke to this, and it stuck with me.
sentences.zh: 拜登总统在国会参众两联席会议上的演讲中有一句话阐述了这一点，让我印象深刻。

sentences.en: He spoke of the need for the United States to come together to confront China.
sentences.zh: 他谈到了美国需要团结起来对抗中国。

sentences.en: And, you know, Michael, the State of the Union speech was just the culmination of several moments at which President Biden had raised this concept,
sentences.zh: 而且，迈克尔，国情咨文演讲只是拜登总统多次提出这一概念的高潮，

sentences.en: that it was the challenge for the United States to prove that a disorganized, disorderly democracy could get its act together and actually accomplish big things,
sentences.zh: 即美国的挑战在于证明一个混乱不堪的民主政体能够振作起来，真正完成大事，

sentences.en: and that that wasn't simply the pathway that autocracies could take.
sentences.zh: 而这并非只有独裁政体才能走的路。

sentences.en: That has been the closest thing to a Biden national security philosophy that we've heard yet.
sentences.zh: 这是迄今为止我们听到的最接近拜登国家安全哲学的言论。

sentences.en: So perhaps it is worth noting, David, that despite the fact that President Trump and President Biden really don't agree on much of anything,
sentences.zh: 所以也许值得指出的是，大卫，尽管特朗普总统和拜登总统在几乎所有事情上都意见不一，

sentences.en: they do both seem to agree on the threat of China and the need for the United States to invest in such a way that it can counter it.
sentences.zh: 但他们在对中国的威胁以及美国需要进行投资以进行反制的必要性上似乎确实看法一致。

sentences.en: That's absolutely right, Michael.
sentences.zh: 完全正确，迈克尔。

sentences.en: And some of these efforts, including the more than $50 billion for the semiconductor industry, first got passed during the Trump administration.
sentences.zh: 其中一些努力，包括为半导体产业提供的超过500亿美元资金，最初是在特朗普政府时期通过的。

sentences.en: And it is now being rolled into this bill.
sentences.zh: 而现在它正被纳入这项法案中。

sentences.en: There are some cautions here, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，这里也有一些警告。

sentences.en: You have seen this bill get squeezed down a little bit by people who were afraid we were spending too much money.
sentences.zh: 你已经看到这项法案被那些担心我们花钱太多的人稍微压缩了一点。

sentences.en: You have seen some objections that the bill, because it's one of the few spending bills that will actually pass in Congress,
sentences.zh: 你已经听到了一些反对意见，认为该法案因为是国会中少数几个真正能通过的支出法案之一，

sentences.en: has become a Christmas tree for everybody's favorite project.
sentences.zh: 已经变成了每个人安放自己最喜爱项目的圣诞树。

sentences.en: But what we've learned here, essentially, is that the competition with China, the fear of China,
sentences.zh: 但我们在这里学到的基本上是，与中国的竞争、对中国的恐惧、

sentences.en: both the realistic and the exaggerated fears of China, have become the one great unifying element of American politics today.
sentences.zh: 对中国现实和夸大的恐惧，已经成为当今美国政治中唯一的强大统一因素。

sentences.en: And if that is true, David, then I guess there is some hope that a democracy can plan for the long term, that this is not just the terrain of an autocracy.
sentences.zh: 如果这是真的，大卫，那么我想我们还有一些希望，即民主政体可以为长远做规划，这不仅是独裁政体的专利。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Now, even after this bill passes, our research and development spending as a percentage of our GDP is still going to be well below the Chinese and some other countries.
sentences.zh: 现在，即使在这项法案通过之后，我们占GDP比例的研发支出仍将远低于中国和其他一些国家。

sentences.en: It is more of a start.
sentences.zh: 这更像是一个开始。

sentences.en: But if there's one key lesson that emerges from the debate, really the non-debate over this bill,
sentences.zh: 但如果说从这场辩论（实际上是对该法案的非辩论）中浮现出一个关键教训，

sentences.en: it's that America needs, again, as it always has, an adversary to be the organizing thought for things we probably needed to do anyway.
sentences.zh: 那就是美国再次需要（正如它一直以来那样）一个对手，来作为我们无论如何都可能需要去做的事情的组织思想。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: First Russia, now China.
sentences.zh: 先是俄罗斯，现在是中国。

sentences.en: Russia in the Cold War, China in the New Cold War.
sentences.zh: 冷战中的俄罗斯，新冷战中的中国。

sentences.en: That's how America gets its act together.
sentences.zh: 这就是美国振作起来的方式。

sentences.en: That's how America has a shot at getting its act together.
sentences.zh: 这就是美国有机会振作起来的方式。

sentences.en: Well, David, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好吧，大卫，非常感谢。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们非常感激。

sentences.en: Thank you, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: We are deeply sorry for the impact that this attack had.
sentences.zh: 对于这次袭击产生的影响，我们深表歉意。

sentences.en: But we are also heartened by the resilience of our country and of our company.
sentences.zh: 但我们也为我们国家和公司的韧性感到鼓舞。

sentences.en: During a Senate hearing on Tuesday,
sentences.zh: 在周二举行的一场参议院听证会上，

sentences.en: the chief executive of Colonial Pipeline apologized for the consequences of a ransomware attack that cut off energy access to much of the East Coast last month.
sentences.zh: Colonial Pipeline（殖民地管道公司）的首席执行官就上个月导致东海岸大部分地区能源供应中断的勒索软件攻击后果进行了道歉。

sentences.en: I made the decision to pay, and I made the decision to keep the information about the payment as confidential as possible.
sentences.zh: 我做出了支付的决定，我也做出了尽可能对支付信息保密的决定。

sentences.en: The executive, Joseph Blunt, defended his controversial decision to pay hackers more than $4 million in ransom to end the attack and bring a major fuel pipeline back online.
sentences.zh: 这位高管约瑟夫·布朗特（Joseph Blunt）为他颇具争议的决定进行了辩护，即向黑客支付超过400万美元的赎金，以结束攻击并让一条主要的燃料管道重新上线。

sentences.en: It was the hardest decision I've made in my 39 years in the energy industry, and I know how critical our pipeline is to the country, and I put the interests of the country firSt.
sentences.zh: 这是我在能源行业39年里做过的最艰难的决定，我知道我们的管道对国家有多么重要，我把国家的利益放在了第一位。

sentences.en: And data from the Internal Revenue Service, obtained by the news organization ProPublica, shows that between 2014 and 2018, the 25 richest Americans, including Jeff Bezos,
sentences.zh: 新闻机构ProPublica获取的美国国税局数据显示，在2014年至2018年期间，包括杰夫·贝佐斯在内的25位最富有的美国人，

sentences.en: Michael Bloomberg, and Elon Musk, paid little and, in some years, no federal income taxes.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔·布隆伯格和埃隆·马斯克缴纳的联邦所得税极少，甚至在某些年份没有缴纳。

sentences.en: ProPublica found that the billionaires avoided paying significant income tax by exploiting loopholes and deductions in the tax code, by borrowing large sums of money,
sentences.zh: ProPublica发现，亿万富翁们通过利用税法中的漏洞和扣除额、通过借入巨额资金，

sentences.en: and because the United States emphasizes taxing traditional income over accumulated wealth, such as stocks and real estate.
sentences.zh: 以及因为美国更强调对传统收入而非股票和房地产等累积财富征税，从而避免了支付巨额所得税。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Asla Chaturvedi, Eric Krupke, Luke Vanderpleen, and Nina Patak.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由 Asla Chaturvedi、Eric Krupke、Luke Vanderpleen 和 Nina Patak 制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Dave Shaw, engineered by Chris Wood, and contains original music by Marian Lozano and Dan Powell.
sentences.zh: 由 Dave Shaw 编辑，Chris Wood 混音，并包含 Marian Lozano 和 Dan Powell 的原创音乐。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是本期《The Daily》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受到严密控制的机器在运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了一批自诩为改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党就一直陷入一场残酷、混乱、有时又令人兴奋的争斗之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的 Metro 节目中，我和萨拉·科尼格（Sarah Koenig）将为您讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: Metro。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在您获取播客的任何地方收听。
